newsitem.title: UK: CRESTCo to reschedule UK settlement transition.
newsitem.headline: CRESTCo to reschedule UK settlement transition.

text.p: The transition of around 10 FTSE 100 securities to CREST, the new electronic settlement system, is to be rescheduled from next month to 1997 after software "teething problems', CRESTCo, the Bank of England led-group developing the system, said on Wednesday. The delay will reduce the increase in settlement volumes planned for December and create a breathing space to allow CRESTCo to eliminate backlogs currently being experienced.

CRESTCo said it will continue to monitor the performance both of its own system and that of its users over the coming weeks and would consider whether to extend the rescheduling for securities planned to move onto CREST in January 1997.
CREST software has been experiencing what have been described as "teething problems' which surfaced once volumes in the system increased.
CRESTCo hopes to rectify the most significant of these in the coming two to three weeks.

The paperless CREST system was developed to replace the London Stock Exchange's Talisman settlement system and securities have been moved to CREST in a series of weekly batches with volumes being built up over a period of time.
CREST settles over 10,000 transactions per day, accounting for around 25 percent of the total market volume of bargains.

A number of users have also experienced problems in the introduction of the new system and are keen to improve their own familiarity with how to operate Crest before volumes increase further, CrestCo said.
